title: I Let the Condo Board's Quiet Hours Catch Their Own Party

parts.text: I stood in the hallway at 1:12 a.m. counting subwoofer hits. I am thirty-one, night-shift adjacent, trying to sleep before a 6 a.m. clock-in. The party was in the board president's unit, Dana. Dana had fined me in March for a blender at 10:01 p.m. The hallway carpet smelled like steam-cleaned fish, a mystery. My neighbor Hasan recorded a decibel app with me. Dana said, "It's a board social" I said, "The packet doesn't list exceptions" The welcome packet quiet hours: 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The subwoofer is still going, and my March blender fine is in the same PDF as her party.

parts.text: Hasan and I submitted the clip and the March fine side by side. The management company, allergic to irony, voided my blender fine and dinged Dana's unit. She called it a coup. It was a PDF. The next social ended at 9:40 with a playlist that sounded sorry. I slept. The fish smell faded, or I adapted. Hasan got a plant as a thank-you, which he did not want. I still blend at 9:50, legally, joylessly, banana, protein, rage. Quiet hours are only real if they bite the president. Management said, "Both files received" Dana said, "This is targeted" Dana waves tightly. I wave like a blender. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.
